summary: Client connection aborts during sustained high-max_tokens burst when history compaction runs
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated client-side connection aborts (socket closed) during multi-minute generation jobs that request large max_tokens (>=120k) in a sustained burst pattern. The aborts align with background history compaction events on the Dedicated pool and appear to cause the runtime to drop the HTTP/2 stream rather than returning a structured 5xx. Impact: customer workflows time out after 60-120s, generation partially returned then aborted; downstream system marks the request failed and retries leading to increased cost and queue pressure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure an account on dedicated pool with gptx-13b pinned. 2) Send a series of streaming generation requests at t=0..N spaced 1s apart, each with 'max_tokens': 120000 and a multi-turn conversation preamble (~80k tokens). 3) Observe after ~90-150s that the client receives a TCP FIN/RST and the stream terminates prematurely. 4) Repeat with history_compaction enabled on session (default for this customer's deployment); issue appears reproducible within 3-8 requests in a sustained burst.
observed_behavior: HTTP/2 stream abruptly closes from the server side with no final chunk or error JSON. Customer logs show 'stream reset by peer' and runtime logs show 'worker aborted due to compaction pause' around the same timestamps. The API gateway reports 499/stream_reset counts rather than 504 or 5xx.
expected_behavior: For large-generation requests, runtime should either: return a proper 5xx error with retryable flag, stream partial outputs and a graceful termination, or honor the client timeout with a 504. It should not drop the connection without diagnostic payloads.
logs:
[2026-03-10T14:11:02Z] request_id=ae3f4d: start generation, max_tokens=120000, seq_len=80000
[2026-03-10T14:12:34Z] compaction: session_id=xxc-99 triggered history_compaction start
[2026-03-10T14:12:34Z] worker=slot-17: pausing emission for compaction (estimated 1.6s)
[2026-03-10T14:12:35Z] gateway: http2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) for request_id=ae3f4d
[2026-03-10T14:12:35Z] runtime: worker slot-17 crashed with SIGABRT (oom=false)
[2026-03-10T14:12:36Z] scheduler: requeued request ae3f4d -> queue depth spike observed
Customer error: client-side: 'StreamResetError: stream closed by server during chunk 42'
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: history_compaction holds a lock and triggers a synchronous serialization path that blocks token emission long enough for the gateway to drop the stream.
- Reproduced on a dedicated pool replica in staging with identical autoscaling config: compaction event correlated with stream resets.
- Heap profiles show increased GC and a blocking mutex in session-serializer during compaction.
- Worker logs indicate compaction pause timers sometimes spike to 1.8s under sustained burst; gateway max stream idle configured to 1.5s in this cluster.
- Eng analysis: compaction path performs blocking I/O on main worker thread which should be offloaded to a background thread.
- Related historical tickets show similar symptoms but those were tied to KV serialization spikes (see linked issues).
workaround: 1) Customer temporary mitigation: reduce 'max_tokens' to <=40k and lower burst concurrency; disable history_compaction at session creation (session param history_compaction=false) until patch applied. 2) Cluster config workaround: increase http2 stream idle timeout to 3s for this dedicated pool (applied as targeted override).
resolution: In progress - engineering has a patch that offloads history compaction to a background worker and adds non-blocking snapshots. Patch landed in PR #4382 and staged to canary pool on 2026-03-12. Verification steps: run sustained high-max_tokens workload for 1h and confirm no stream resets during compaction windows. Final rollout scheduled after a dark launch window.
next_steps:
- SRE to monitor canary pool for 48h after dark launch (alerts set for RST_STREAM spikes).
- If stable, schedule controlled rollout to all dedicated pools on 2026-03-15.
- Product to coordinate communication to affected customers and offer one-time credits for retries.
- Postmortem doc to be created after resolution and linked in this ticket.
